_meta.description: Disposal recommendations per class (PLAN.md Section 9). Edit bins and wording here; no code changes needed.

uncertain.title: Not sure - check before you throw
uncertain.rule: When in doubt, keep it out of recycling and ask a staff member.
advice: Compare the item with the two most likely categories below.
If it is dirty, mixed-material or you still cannot tell, use the Black general waste bin.
Never put anything that might be a battery or electronic item in general waste.

unrecognised.title: Could not recognise this item
advice: Place the item on a plain, uncluttered background.
Make the item fill most of the frame.
Use good, even lighting and avoid strong shadows or glare.
Photograph one item at a time.

steps: Keep it dry and clean
Remove plastic windows, tape and staples where easy
Flatten or fold to save space
do_not: Do not recycle greasy or food-soiled paper (napkins, pizza paper) - use the Green bin
Do not include wax-coated or plastic-laminated paper
paper.impact_note: Recycling paper saves trees, water and energy compared with making new paper.

steps: Flatten boxes completely
Remove tape, labels and any plastic packing material if possible
Keep it dry
do_not: Do not recycle wet or food-soaked cardboard
Do not leave polystyrene or bubble wrap inside the box
cardboard.impact_note: Flattened, clean cardboard is one of the most valuable recyclables on campus.

steps: Empty and rinse the container
Remove the cap and label if possible
Flatten bottles
do_not: Do not put food-soiled plastic in the recycling bin
Do not include chip packets or multi-layer wrappers - they go in general waste
plastic.impact_note: Clean plastic can be recycled instead of going to landfill.

steps: Empty and rinse cans and tins
Put loose lids inside the can
Keep aerosol cans separate and only recycle them when fully empty
do_not: Do not crush cans with sharp edges by hand
Do not include batteries or electronics - they go to e-waste
metal.impact_note: Aluminium and steel can be recycled indefinitely without losing quality.

steps: Empty and rinse bottles and jars
Remove metal or plastic lids
Wrap broken glass in paper or cardboard before disposal and label it
do_not: Do not handle broken glass with bare hands
Do not include mirrors, window glass, light bulbs or ceramics
glass.impact_note: Glass is fully recyclable and remelting it uses less energy than making new glass.

steps: Food scraps, fruit and vegetable peels, tea leaves and garden waste only
Drain excess liquid first
do_not: Do not include plastic bags, wrappers or cutlery
Do not include cooking oil in large amounts
organic.impact_note: Separated food waste can be composted instead of producing methane in landfill.

steps: Take it to the campus e-waste collection point
Tape over the terminals of lithium and 9V batteries
Keep damaged or swollen batteries separate and tell a staff member
do_not: Never put batteries in general waste or recycling bins - they can start fires
Do not puncture, crush or burn batteries
battery.impact_note: Batteries contain toxic and valuable metals that can be recovered safely.

steps: Donate clean, usable clothes and shoes
Tie pairs of shoes together
Put worn-out textiles in a bag in the dry waste bin
do_not: Do not donate wet, mouldy or heavily soiled items
Do not put textiles in the wet waste bin
textile.impact_note: Reusing one garment avoids the water and energy needed to make a new one.

steps: Use this bin only when the item cannot be recycled
Bag loose waste to keep the bin clean
do_not: Do not put batteries, electronics or hazardous items here
Do not put recyclables here if they can be cleaned
general.impact_note: General waste goes to landfill, so it is the last resort.
